## A cache for the course search {.hero-title}

Priya Rao, platform team

::: notes
Cue: thanks, then the wait at nine
Thank you to the platform team for the time today.
Every morning at nine, three thousand students open the course search, and the page slows to a crawl.
We cut that wait to under a second, and the fix came from one fact about how students search.
:::

## Sam and Lee built the cache with me

Sam Okafor and Lee Chen, platform team

::: notes
Cue: credit the team
Sam and Lee built this with me, and the registration office gave us four weeks of data.
:::

## Each search page takes eight seconds {data-section="Students wait eight seconds at nine"}

::: {.incremental data-fragment-effect="dim"}
- 3,000 searches in ten minutes
- 8 seconds for each page
- 1 in 5 students gives up
:::

::: notes
Cue: the size of the wait
Students wait eight seconds for each search page when registration opens.
That's at nine every morning, when three thousand students search in ten minutes.
One student in five gives up and tries again later.
:::

## A copy for one minute {.section-divider data-section="A copy for one minute"}

::: notes
Cue: the second section
Now the fix.
:::

## Cached pages skip the database {data-section="A copy for one minute"}

::: {.ds-left .ds-media}
![Searches go to a copy in memory, and only the misses reach the database](assets/cache.svg){.ds-fit}
:::

::: {.ds-right .ds-pane .incremental data-fragment-effect="dim"}
- Keep each page for one minute
- Serve the copy to the next student
- Clear the copy when a course changes
:::

::: notes
Cue: one minute; no new server
We keep each result page in memory for one minute.
The next student who asks for the same page gets the copy, with no database read.
When a teacher changes a course, we clear the copies for that course at once.
:::

## Hit rate sets the load {data-section="A copy for one minute" data-step-summary="match"}

::::: {.two-col}
:::: {.equation-steps data-equation-steps="hit-rate|searches" data-step-indices="1|2"}
$$ \text{reads} = (1 - \htmlClass{hit-rate}{h}) \times \htmlClass{searches}{\text{searches}} $$
::::
:::: {.incremental data-fragment-effect="dim"}
[h is the share of searches that find a copy]{.fragment data-fragment-index="1" data-match="hit-rate"}

[Each search that misses reads the database]{.fragment data-fragment-index="2" data-match="searches"}
::::
:::::

::: notes
Cue: define the hit rate; then the searches; the colors together
The number of database reads is the share of searches that miss the cache, times the number of searches.
We call the share that finds a copy the hit rate.
At a hit rate of nine in ten, the database does one tenth of the work.
:::
